executiveSummary: Surveillance reports from ECDC and PAHO spanning November 2025 through May 2026 indicate multiple concurrent disease threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1), a BSL-3 select agent, has generated repeated epidemiological updates in the Americas region, signaling sustained zoonotic spillover risk. Additional threats include active mpox transmission, dengue surges, yellow fever activity, and the onset of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season coinciding with RSV co-circulation. Pertussis resurgence and measles importation risks in the Americas further compound the multi-pathogen burden.
bottomLine: The Americas face a complex multi-pathogen threat landscape dominated by H5N1 zoonotic risk, mpox spread, dengue surge, and vaccine-preventable disease resurgence, requiring coordinated regional surveillance and response.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained zoonotic activity
Repeated alerts suggest ongoing animal-to-human spillover risk across multiple countries in the Americas
BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential if sustained human-to-human transmission emerges
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance at animal-human interface; ensure antiviral stockpile readiness; strengthen poultry worker PPE and monitoring protocols

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 2026 confirming ongoing transmission in the Americas
Sustained circulation following 2022-2024 global outbreak trajectory
Potential for clade IIb and emerging clade Ib co-circulation increasing diagnostic complexity
threats.action: Reinforce ring vaccination strategies; expand diagnostic capacity for clade differentiation; strengthen contact tracing in affected communities

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update February 2026 indicating elevated case counts
Americas historically records highest global dengue burden with 2024-2025 record surge trajectory continuing
Risk of severe dengue and healthcare system strain in endemic countries
threats.action: Intensify vector control operations; activate early warning systems for severe dengue; ensure clinical management guidelines are current at facility level

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 2026 indicating active transmission risk
Ongoing epizootics in non-human primates serve as sentinel indicators of human risk
Vaccination coverage gaps in at-risk populations in endemic zones
threats.action: Audit vaccination coverage in endemic and border regions; strengthen epizootic surveillance in non-human primates; ensure vaccine availability for travelers and endemic populations

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two PAHO epidemiological updates issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained resurgence
Pattern consistent with global post-COVID pertussis rebound due to immunity gaps
Infants and under-immunized adolescents at highest risk of severe disease
threats.action: Review childhood immunization coverage data; promote Tdap booster programs for adolescents and pregnant women; strengthen laboratory confirmation capacity

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and RSV Co-circulation
signals: PAHO alert April 2026 marking start of Southern Hemisphere influenza season
January 2026 alert flagged simultaneous influenza and RSV circulation straining pediatric healthcare capacity
December 2025 alert on Northern Hemisphere season onset indicating global respiratory virus pressure
threats.action: Promote influenza vaccination campaigns ahead of Southern Hemisphere peak; ensure RSV prophylaxis availability for high-risk infants; prepare healthcare surge capacity

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating importation and transmission risk
Post-pandemic immunization gaps have lowered herd immunity thresholds in several countries
Risk of outbreaks in under-vaccinated communities and migrant populations
threats.action: Conduct supplementary immunization activities in high-risk districts; strengthen case-based surveillance and rapid response capacity; verify vaccination status at borders and in migrant settings

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating active transmission
Co-circulation with dengue in Aedes aegypti endemic zones complicates clinical differentiation
Risk of spread to new geographic areas with competent vector populations
threats.action: Enhance arboviral syndromic surveillance to differentiate chikungunya from dengue; strengthen vector control; educate clinicians on chronic chikungunya arthropathy management

selectAgentSummary: Avian Influenza A(H5N1) is a BSL-3 select agent with documented detections triggering two PAHO epidemiological updates in the Americas region (November 2025 and March 2026). The sustained zoonotic activity across the Americas represents the highest biosecurity concern in this surveillance dataset. No BSL-4 pathogen detections were reported in the available reports. H5N1 pandemic preparedness measures, including antiviral stockpiling, enhanced genomic surveillance, and poultry-human interface monitoring, are critically indicated.
amrSignals: No explicit AMR signals reported in available surveillance titles; however, Bordetella pertussis macrolide resistance warrants monitoring given resurgence reports
GLP-1 receptor agonist misuse alert (February 2026) may indirectly signal healthcare system vulnerabilities affecting antimicrobial stewardship capacity
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen surge in the Americas creating compounded healthcare system stress across 2025-2026
Post-pandemic immunity gaps driving resurgence of vaccine-preventable diseases including pertussis and measles
Sustained H5N5 zoonotic spillover events in the Americas suggest expanding geographic range of infected poultry and wild bird populations
Southern Hemisphere influenza season onset coinciding with RSV activity mirrors patterns seen in 2022-2024 that strained pediatric intensive care capacity
Repeated PAHO alerts across multiple arboviruses (dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever) indicate hyperendemic vector-borne disease pressure in Latin America
ECDC issuing consecutive weekly threat reports through April-May 2026 suggests elevated European communicable disease activity requiring continued monitoring
